project.objective: Did Hinrich Burmeister of Schönberg (b. 1653) have a son Hinrich baptised 29 July 1687, and is the 'Elsch Burmeister' named as the child's mother his first wife Liesbeth Oldenburg?

questions.question: Who was the mother of the child Hinrich Burmeister baptised at Schönberg on 29 July 1687, son of Hinrich Burmeister of Schönberg (b. 1653)?
questions.rationale: The objective turns on one child event: the 29 July 1687 baptism of a son Hinrich, whose mother the record names as 'Elsch Burmeister'. The tree has no 1687 baptism. Its only Hinrich son of this couple (P71D-DRJ) is christened 18 Aug 1683 and attached to Liesbeth Oldenburg, who married in Oct 1682 and died 4 Jan 1689, so a 1687 child would fall within her first marriage. Whether the 1683 entry and the 1687 baptism are one child or two is unresolved, and it decides whether the tree's assignment to Liesbeth stands. Naming the mother as the fact asked for lets the answer confirm or refute the identification of Elsch with Liesbeth Oldenburg.

person_evidence.rationale: Mother named 'Elsch Burmeister' at the 29 Jul 1687 baptism (Schönberg). 'Elsch' is a Low German pet form of Elisabeth, the same root as 'Liesbeth/Liesabeth' used for this tree person in the 1682 marriage record (a_021). FamilySearch's Germany Naming Customs wiki confirms dialectal/nickname given-name variants are common in this era/region (illustrated for 'Barbara' with many forms, e.g. Bärbel, Wawerl) though it does not name 'Elsch' specifically. same_person scores this persona only 0.027 against Liesbeth Oldenburg because it compares literal given-name strings, which the dialect variant defeats on its face. Qualitatively: the baptism date (29 Jul 1687) falls within this woman's documented marriage (24 Oct 1682 to her death 4 Jan 1689); the record's father, correlatively identified as her husband Hinrich Burmeister of Schönberg (see note below), is consistent throughout. No contradicting birthplace, birth date, or parent is recorded for her, so no core_identifier_conflict applies. Capped at probable (not confident): the given-name equivalence rests on onomastic plausibility rather than a documented spelling-variant list, and the record's father persona itself could not be formally linked above speculative in this project (he shares his given name with his own father and his own son in the tree; see summary), so this mother identification currently stands on the marriage-window/place correlation alone. This is the project's central open question.

proof_summaries.narrative_markdown:
## Question
Who was the mother of the child Hinrich Burmeister baptised at Schönberg on 29 July 1687, son of Hinrich Burmeister of Schönberg (b. 1653)? The objective has two parts: did Hinrich Burmeister (b. 1653) have a son Hinrich baptised on that date, and is the mother, recorded as "Elsch Burmeister", his first wife Liesbeth Oldenburg?

## Conclusion
The evidence supports, at the **probable** tier, that (1) the child baptised 29 July 1687 was a son of Hinrich Burmeister (b. 30 Nov 1653, tree person G8CJ-7VL), and (2) "Elsch Burmeister" is his wife Liesbeth Oldenburg (GV6M-YN8, recorded in the marriage entry as Liesabeth Ollenborgs). The child is a second son named Hinrich, distinct from the Hinrich christened 18 Aug 1683 (P71D-DRJ).

## Evidence
**The baptism.** The 29 July 1687 Schönberg entry names the child Hinrich Burmeister, the father Hinrich Burmeister and the mother "Elsch Burmeister" ("Deutschland, ausgewählte evangelische Kirchenbücher 1500-1971", FamilySearch, https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:QPV4-RPYG : Sat Jul 26 23:19:35 UTC 2025, Entry for Hinrich Burmeister and Hinrich Burmeister, 29. Juli 1687). Classification: derivative index of the original church register; the information (parentage) is primary, stated by the presenting parent, and direct for the parentage but indirect for the mother's identity as Liesbeth, because the entry gives only a first name and a married surname.

**The marriage.** On 24 Oct 1682 at Schönberg, groom Hinrich Burmeister married Liesabeth Ollenborgs, daughter of Claus Ollenborgs ("Deutschland, ausgewählte evangelische Kirchenbücher 1500-1971", FamilySearch, https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:QPV4-KKZX : Thu Oct 16 07:16:48 UTC 2025, Entry for Hinrich Burmeister and Liesabeth Ollenborgs, 24 Oct 1682). Derivative; primary information given by the parties themselves. The groom matches G8CJ-7VL at similarity 0.994 and the bride matches Liesbeth Oldenburg at 0.987 (Ollenborgs being a genitive/dialect rendering of Oldenburg). Tree fact: Liesbeth Oldenburg's Death on 4 Jan 1689 (Schönberg) means she was alive and married to G8CJ-7VL at the 1687 baptism; his second marriage, to Anna Meyborg, was on 27 Feb 1690.

**Correlation.** The father in the 1687 baptism matches G8CJ-7VL (similarity 0.938; Schönberg; age about 33). The other same-named tree men are excluded by date: P9PK-53N died in 1658 and P71D-DRJ was christened in 1683. "Elsch" is a Low German pet form of Elisabeth, as is Liesbeth, so a man whose recorded wife in 1682 was Liesabeth and whose recorded wife in 1687 was Elsch, in the same parish, had the same wife by the simplest reading. A name-string comparison scores this poorly (0.027) only because the dialect variants differ literally; the FamilySearch Germany Naming Customs wiki confirms such variants are normal but does not list Elsch specifically.

## The competing household
A baptism of another Hinrich Burmeister on 9 May 1687, mother Anna Burmeister (https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:QPV4-2MW3), falls only eleven weeks before the target baptism. The two cannot be children of one mother, and G8CJ-7VL's wife in May 1687 was Liesbeth, not Anna (Anna Meyborg married him only in 1690). That record therefore belongs to a different Hinrich Burmeister household in the same small parish. This is why the father in the July record is identified by the marriage and tree chronology rather than by name alone. It is also the main residual risk: the exclusion rests on the spouse contradiction and on tree dates, not on an independent sponsor, occupation or house-number identification, and no separate Hinrich Burmeister of the right age with a wife named Elsch/Elisabeth has been ruled out by a register search. If the July father were that other man, the identification of Elsch with Liesbeth would fall. Overturn risk is high for that reason.

## The second son
P71D-DRJ (christened 18 Aug 1683, the couple's child) and the 1687 child are different baptisms four years apart. A second son with the same name is consistent with the German custom of reusing the name of a child who died; no burial for P71D-DRJ was found, so that remains open.

## Limitations
All three records are derivative index entries; I did not examine register images. Pending FamilySearch hints, film 69805 images, neighbouring-parish registers, godparent (FAN) evidence, and burial records for the elder son and for Liesbeth (1689) were not reached and could corroborate or overturn the link. No conflict is registered. The finding is probable, not proved, because the mother's identity rests on a name-variant equivalence plus marriage-window consistency, with a named competing household not independently excluded.

quirks: FamilySearch's standard-place record for the Schönberg Lutheran Parish is dated 1701-1871, but the parish's own church book (catalog koha:266682) runs 1640-1875 and so covers the 1687 baptism well before 1701 — trust the catalog record and film dates, not the standard-place date range, when judging coverage for this period.

# Locality Guide: Schönberg, Mecklenburg-Strelitz, Germany (1683–1689)

## Jurisdiction overview
- **Place:** Schönberg, a Lutheran parish/municipality in the district (Amtsgericht) of Schönberg, Mecklenburg-Strelitz, located roughly 16 km east of Lübeck.
- **Note on identity:** FamilySearch's place index lists several Schönberg entries for the Mecklenburg area at different dates (1701–1871 and 1806–1871 for the Ratzeburg/Mecklenburg-Strelitz parish and municipality, 1871–1933 for a later municipality record, and the modern 1994– Nordwestmecklenburg municipality) — these are successive standard-place records for the same town as jurisdictional status changed, not different places.
- **Parent jurisdiction (period):** Mecklenburg-Strelitz.
- **Key historical context:** The period 1683–1689 falls within the post-Thirty Years' War recovery era in Mecklenburg; Lutheran parish record-keeping was already well established at Schönberg by this date (the surviving church book begins in 1640).

## Boundary changes
The FamilySearch place database shows Schönberg's jurisdictional label changing over time (parish 1701–1871, municipality 1806–1871, municipality 1871–1933, modern municipality 1994–) while its physical location and lat/long are constant. No tool result in this survey identifies an actual territorial split or re-parenting of Schönberg itself during 1683–1689; the parish's own record series (1640–1875) runs continuously through the target window.

## Available record types

### Church records (the record type that matters for this inquiry)
- **Denomination:** Evangelische Kirche (Lutheran), the only denomination this survey found recorded for Schönberg.
- **Record types:** The parish's Kirchenbuch (catalog entry koha:266682, creator "Evangelische Kirche Schönberg (AG. Schönberg, Mecklenburg-Strelitz)") covers baptisms (Taufen), marriages (Heiraten), burials (Tote) and confirmations (Konfirmationen), 1640–1875.
- **Microfilms:** Six films split the run by date and record type — film 69805 "Taufen 1640-1749" (imageGroupNumber 102151198) is the one covering a 29 July 1687 baptism; film 69807 "Taufen, Tote 1642-1809, Heiraten 1640-1809" (imageGroupNumber 102151200) also spans 1687 for burials and marriages. Later films (69806, 69808-69810) cover 1750 onward and are out of scope for this inquiry.
- **Where held:** FamilySearch's catalog marks this title available at the Granite Mountain Record Vault, the FamilySearch Library, and Online — the catalog entry (koha:266682) states "Online" availability for these microfilmed images.
- **Indexed collection:** The collections_search result "Germany, Mecklenburg-Strelitz, Catholic and Lutheran Church Records, 1664-1937" (FamilySearch collection id 4132032, 440,965 persons) spans 1664–1937 and overlaps the target period; this is almost certainly an index/image set drawn from the same parish films, including Schönberg's, and should be searched by name first.
- **Gaps:** This survey found no indication the 1640–1875 Kirchenbuch has gaps; no wiki page or catalog note states any loss for this specific parish.
- **Language:** German (Kirchenbuch entries of this period are typically German, sometimes with Latin terms).

### Census records
No civil or state census existed in Mecklenburg-Strelitz in the 1680s; this record type is inapplicable to the target period.

### Probate and court records
No catalog or collection result specific to Schönberg probate/court records surfaced in this survey. The Germany Research Tips page (country level) notes German probate-relevant actions (bequests, inheritance) were often recorded in local court records ("Schuld- und Pfandprotokolle") rather than a dedicated probate series — consult the regional state archive for Mecklenburg-Strelitz if needed.

Not surveyed in detail for this inquiry; no tool result returned land records specific to Schönberg for 1683–1689.

### Cemetery records
No FindAGrave or BillionGraves coverage for 17th-century Schönberg burials was returned; burials of this date would be in the parish Kirchenbuch itself (Tote series), not a separate cemetery record.

Not applicable — no newspapers existed in 1680s Mecklenburg-Strelitz.

Not applicable to the research question at hand (a 1687 baptism); no port-of-entry or passenger records bear on this locality/period.

## Repository guide

### Online repositories

| FamilySearch | Catalog entry koha:266682 (Kirchenbuch 1640-1875, 6 films, marked "Online"); collection id 4132032 "Germany, Mecklenburg-Strelitz, Catholic and Lutheran Church Records, 1664-1937" (440,965 persons) | Both are the primary and (likely) only route to the 1687 baptism itself | Free |

**Coverage of this survey:** `volume_search` scoped to the Schönberg Lutheran Parish standard place returned 0 digitized volumes (likely because the digitized/indexed breakdown is filed under the broader Mecklenburg-Strelitz place, not the parish-specific standard place); `catalog_search` confirms the relevant Kirchenbuch and its six films directly. A broader `volume_search` on Mecklenburg-Strelitz, Germany for 1680-1690 returned 40 matching volumes/coverages, of which this response detailed the first page (10); the Schönberg Taufen film specifically was not among that first page, so the full set was not examined for a volume_search match to the exact parish film.

This survey found no record series for Schönberg that are confirmed offline-only; the Kirchenbuch for the target period is marked "Online" in the catalog.

## Known record losses
No tool result in this survey states any loss for the Schönberg Kirchenbuch; the series is continuous 1640–1875 per the catalog.

## Research tips
- All German records are organized in the FamilySearch catalog by their 1871 place name, so Schönberg appears under Mecklenburg-Strelitz in the catalog rather than any later or current province name (https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Germany_Research_Tips_and_Strategies).
- Work from the known to the unknown and document each generation's births via church records before relying on the tree (https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Germany_Getting_Started).
- Check witnesses at a baptism — they are often relatives and can resolve ambiguity between same-named individuals in the same parish (https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Germany_Research_Tips_and_Strategies).
- Because the FamilySearch Wiki's `home`, `getting_started`, `online_records`, and `research_tips` pages have no dedicated Schönberg/Mecklenburg-Strelitz-level article (the parish-level `home` page returned "No wiki page found"), the country-level Germany pages are the best available guidance; consult the Mecklenburg-Strelitz GenWiki page (http://wiki-de.genealogy.net/Mecklenburg-Strelitz) for more local detail.
- Given the neighboring parishes listed in the catalog search under the same AG. Schönberg jurisdiction (Herrnburg, Carlow, Selmsdorf, Demern, Domhof Ratzeburg, Schlagsdorf, Ziethen), search these adjoining parish Kirchenbücher if the 1687 baptism is not found in Schönberg's own register, since families sometimes used a neighboring church.
- Search the collection "Germany, Mecklenburg-Strelitz, Catholic and Lutheran Church Records, 1664-1937" (FamilySearch collection 4132032) by name first, since it is indexed and may surface the Hinrich Burmeister baptism without browsing film 69805 image by image.
